pages.name: What still runs?
pages.task: Both compressors stop. Do the tools still get air?
pages.answer: Yes, for a while, from the receiver
pages.why: R1 is a tank of air under pressure. With both compressors stopped, it still feeds the header. Its pressure falls as the users take air. Then the users stop. So R1 counts as a source until it runs down.

pages.name: Four steps
pages.text: Read a sheet you have never seen in four steps. Find the legend, then every source. Then find the state it is drawn in. Last, trace one path at a time. Legend lights the key. Sources rings C1, C2 and R1. State lights Note 1 and the N.C. marks. Trace lights the path from C1 through R1 and V3 to the tools.

pages.name: One path at a time
pages.text: On a control sheet, trace one path at a time, from the supply line to a coil. Then find each contact by its tag, wherever it is drawn. One part can act on several paths. Path 1 is bold from L through -S10, -F11, -S11, -B11 and -K12's contact to coil -K11. -K11's contact in path 2 opens. Its contact in path 3 closes. So -Y11 lifts the brake, and the hook rises.

pages.name: What if the top limit opens?
pages.task: The hook has reached the top, so -B11 is open. You hold Up, then Down. What happens?
pages.answer: Up does nothing, and Down still works
pages.why: -B11 sits only in path 1. Once open, it breaks the path to -K11. So Up does nothing. Path 2 does not pass it, so -K12 still pulls in. -K12's contact in path 3 feeds -Y11. So the brake lifts for the way down.

pages.name: Isolate the receiver
pages.task: You must open receiver R1 for an inspection. Which valves do you shut?
pages.answer: V1, V2 and V3, with V7 kept shut
pages.why: Air comes into R1 from the compressors, through V1 and V2, and leaves for the header through V3. Shut all three, and every path to R1 stops at a shut valve. V7 would join R1's inlet line to the header. So check it stays shut. R1 still holds air under pressure. Vent it through V8 before you open it.

pages.name: Every way in
pages.task: You must work on pump -M3's starter, so you lock off -Q13. What else must you lock off before you start?
pages.why: -M3 hangs from section A through -Q13, and from section B through -Q23. -Q23 is open as drawn. But once -Q13 is open, the interlock lets someone at the board close -Q23 to keep the pump running. So find every way in, not just the usual one. Lock off both, then prove it dead at the starter.

pages.answer: Each direction needs its limit switch closed and the other contactor out. Either contactor lifts the brake.
pages.why: A good report says what each path needs and what each coil does. Up needs -B11 closed and -K12 out. Down needs -B12 closed and -K11 out. So the two contactors never pull in together. Either one lifts the brake through path 3. So the hook moves only while a button is held.

Each button drives the hook its own way. The limit switches stop it at each end.
Each button feeds its own coil. The brake holds the hook while it moves.

pages.name: Sheet and plant
pages.task: You plan to cut off the header and its users by shutting V3. Compare the plant with the sheet. Is V3 enough?
pages.answer: No, the plant has a way round V3
pages.why: Where a part sits does not change what it is joined to. What matters is the untagged pipe from R1 to the hose point. It is a way in that the sheet does not show. With V3 shut, R1 still feeds the hose point, and back through V6 the whole header. Check every isolation point on the plant against the sheet. Then report the difference, so the sheet is put right.
